messages:
julia: Quick triage note: after enabling global activation clipping during PTQ for reranker-large we observe a Precision@1 (P@1) regression on a long-tail cohort. NDCG@10 basically flat, but top-1 accuracy is down ~8%. filing here so we can track experiments.

julia: Slice: queries where token_global_freq <= 5 AND query_len <= 6 (rare token short queries). Model: reranker-large-int8-clip6.pt (global clip=6.0). Eval harness command I used below.

```bash
./eval_harness run \
  --model reranker-large \
  --weights /mnt/models/reranker-large/int8/clip6.pt \
  --dataset longtail_holdout.jsonl \
  --slice "token_freq<=5 and query_len<=6" \
  --metrics p@1,ndcg@10,mrr@10 \
  --seed 1234 \
  --query_format preserve_case
```

sanjay: can you paste the before/after numbers (float) so we can see magnitudes? also which runner (cuda vs cpu) and determinism flags?

julia: quick summary (baseline float32 -> quant int8 clip6):
- p@1: 0.340 -> 0.313 (delta -7.9%)
- ndcg@10: 0.718 -> 0.714 (delta -0.6%)
- mrr@10: 0.441 -> 0.432 (delta -2.0%)
runner: cuda, deterministic run flags on.

anya: interesting. pattern where p@1 drops more than ndcg suggests top-1 shuffling. activation clipping could compress high logits for rare tokens and make ties more likely. Did you check tokenization for the failing qids? are they rare surface forms or punctuation variants?

julia: grabbed a few flip examples (qid list small): qid 33021 "xylo-zyme" -> baseline top1 correct, clip6 top1 wrong; qid 33102 "QmR_439" -> similar. Tokenization snippets below.

```
# qid 33021 tokens (baseline): ["xylo", "-", "zyme"]
# qid 33021 tokens (lowercased): ["xylo", "-", "zyme"]
# qid 33102 tokens: ["QmR_", "439"]
```

sanjay: those look like rare subword boundaries and punctuation. Clipping may be zeroing out large activations that disambiguate rare subwords. If top-1 relies on a few high-scoring features, reducing dynamic range hurts P@1.

julia: agreed. planned experiments: 1) sweep clip thresholds {8.0,6.0,4.0} to see monotonicity, 2) try per-channel (per-row) clipping instead of global, 3) hybrid profile: keep embedding + first attention projection as fp16 (protect early signal), 4) run CPU runner to rule out kernel differences. I've queued three jobs: 5250012345-jobA (clip8), jobB (per-channel clip6), jobC (hybrid-embed-fp16).

eval-bot: Jobs submitted: 5250012345-jobA, 5250012345-jobB, 5250012345-jobC. Logs + outputs will appear under /runs/5250012345/* when complete.

anya: additionally, let's compute dot-product histograms between query and positive candidate before vs after clipping. if the tail mass (>99th percentile) shrinks significantly that's a smoking gun. can someone add that diagnostic to the eval job?

julia: added histogram export to jobA/B. also exporting per-example top5 logits for the flip qids so we can inspect rank margins.

sanjay: long-term action: add a "longtail_p@1" gate to quant preflight smoke tests. if p@1 delta > 2% for token_freq<=5 slice we fail the quant profile. also add a tiny 1k mixed rare-surface query prime set to the nightly smoke.

julia: yes will open a PR for the quant-checklist and include suggested thresholds. posting results back in this thread once jobs complete. :eyes:
